clue.text: Liberal's comic — phoney person who leaves the less well-off behind?

definitions.text: person who leaves the less well-off behind?

indicators.note: something phoney is fake, not genuine, so the letters before it are not to be taken in their real order

parts.note: the thirteen letters of the two words, possessive s included

explanation.surface: A comedian from the Liberal party is mocked as a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'Liberal's comic' look like the subject being described; it is only raw material for rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone striving to rise in society tends to drop poorer friends once they move up the ladder.

clue.text: Flags code of behaviour

definitions.meaning: first meaning: banners carried on poles, as by regiments
second meaning: moral principles a person lives by

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flags' looks like a verb (tires, weakens), but it is a plural noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Regimental banners are called this, and so are the principles of conduct someone keeps to.

clue.text: First of children to hang around, one holding on to mum maybe?

definitions.text: one holding on to mum maybe?

indicators.note: first of tells us to keep only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the initial letter of children
to linger is to hang around, loitering

explanation.surface: A child who hangs about at the start of the day, clutching their mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinging person grips tightly, as a small child grips a parent; mum is just one example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Terribly sad poet, alone, powerless, not sure what to do

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters end up in a mangled order
power is abbreviated P in physics, so being without power means dropping that letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A miserable lonely poet, losing their energy, has no idea what to do next.
explanation.walkthrough: Take P (power) out of SAD POET ALONE and rearrange the eleven letters left to make AT A LOOSE END.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at a loose end means having nothing to occupy you and no clear plan.

clue.text: Old king engaging divine cook

indicators.note: to engage something is to take it in and hold it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme
DD is Doctor of Divinity, the degree held by a divine

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch hires a holy man as his chef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' is a noun here, a clergyman, and DD is the abbreviation for his degree. CO(DD)LE.
explanation.definitionFit: To coddle eggs is to cook them gently in water just below boiling point.

clue.text: I travel around north European country, heading off in state of bliss?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: around means one piece wraps the other on both sides

parts.note: to go is to travel
N is the abbreviation for north

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, and off says to remove it

parts.note: a European country

explanation.surface: A traveller circles north and lands up in a European nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark points to the proverb 'ignorance is bliss', so bliss here is one example of the state, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'where ignorance is bliss, 'tis folly to be wise' makes not knowing a happy condition.

clue.text: Use far too much bread?

parts.note: surface reading: eating an excessive amount of loaves; setter's reading: bread is slang for money, so this is spending more than the funds available

explanation.walkthrough: Bread is old slang for money; to exhaust a casino's or anyone's funds is to ruin them financially.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to cost more than can be afforded, using up all the money there is.

clue.text: Rich Greek character has new kitchen device

parts.note: rolling in it means very rich, so rolling is wealthy
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A wealthy Greek man buys a new gadget for his kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person, but it is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A cylinder rolled across dough to flatten it is a standard piece of baking equipment.

clue.text: Sign of unity between partners in business, say

definitions.text: Sign of unity between partners in business, say

parts.words: Sign of unity between partners in business, say
parts.note: surface reading: a gesture such as a handshake showing business partners are together; setter's reading: a printed symbol placed between the names of firms like Marks and Spencer

explanation.walkthrough: Company names joining two partners are often written with the symbol &, which literally unites them on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: The & symbol stands for 'and', the word that joins two things together, as in firm names.

clue.text: Church music ignoring scripture? Excuse me!

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: an anthem is a choral piece sung in church
NT is the New Testament, part of scripture

explanation.surface: A choir piece without its Bible reading, interrupted by someone politely coughing.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove NT from ANTHEM.
explanation.definitionFit: The little throat-clearing noise is made to attract attention, much as someone says 'pardon me'.

clue.text: Pre Napoleon's win, a terrible historical conflict

indicators.note: something terrible is a mess, so the preceding letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the sixteen letters of these words

explanation.surface: Before Napoleon's victory came a dreadful war from history.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon sets the solver thinking of Waterloo or Austerlitz; the war is far older.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the long war between Athens and Sparta in ancient Greece, fifth century BC.

clue.text: Cunning plans soldier finally employs

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the last letter of soldier
to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: A soldier eventually puts some crafty schemes into action.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruses are tricks or stratagems designed to deceive an opponent.

clue.text: Disturbed, thanks to being led by a soldier

indicators.note: being led by means the following pieces walk behind, so they go at the front

parts.note: A plus GI, an American soldier
ta is informal British for thank you
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone upset, owing gratitude to the soldier in charge of them.
explanation.walkthrough: GI is an American enlisted soldier; TA is a British way of saying thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitato is the musical direction for playing in a restless, agitated, troubled manner.

clue.text: Old illustration of tragedy with Europe being torn apart

indicators.note: something torn apart is broken up, and its letters can be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A picture depicting disaster as the continent is ripped to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An early photographic image on a silvered plate, invented by Louis Daguerre in the 1830s.

clue.text: Dog rescuers on the road carrying equipment

parts.note: the Automobile Association, the British breakdown service that rescues stranded motorists
kit is gear or equipment

explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's main roadside breakdown service. A(KIT)A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Akita is a large Japanese breed of spitz-type hound.

clue.text: All decline perversely to accept large invention of physicist

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so a letter is placed inside
acting perversely means going the wrong way, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange ALL DECLINE to DANIEL CELL, then slip L into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: John Frederic Daniell, a British chemist and physicist, devised this early electric battery in 1836.

clue.text: Celebrate outside with jazzy music

indicators.note: outside means one piece sits around the other

parts.note: to sing is to celebrate in song

explanation.surface: A party held outdoors with lively jazz playing.

explanation.definitionFit: Swing is a big-band jazz style of the 1930s and 1940s with a strong rhythmic lilt.

clue.text: Spiritual band?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians, but it is a strip encircling the neck of a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: The stiff white collar worn by clergy is jokingly named after the band round a pet's neck.

clue.text: Danger when last character comes forward presenting dagger

indicators.note: the final letter moves to the front while the others keep their order

parts.note: risk is danger or hazard

explanation.surface: Peril arises when the last person steps forward with a knife.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the K of RISK to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A kris is a Malay or Indonesian short blade with a wavy edge.

clue.text: A job had for one leaving the fold

parts.note: taken as written
a post is a job or position
had a meal means ate

explanation.surface: A position held by someone who has quit the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had' as in had lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate renounces their religion, straying from the flock as a sheep leaves the fold.

clue.text: See an object bringing detestation

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
the indefinite article
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: Seeing a particular item fills someone with hatred.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathing and detestation are both intense dislike or disgust, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Least known artist ahead of others

indicators.note: ahead of says the first piece is placed before the second

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
the rest are the others

explanation.surface: The most obscure painter is ranked above all the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extremely uncommon is seldom seen, so it is the least familiar.

clue.text: Given a chance to do business favourably where customers come in?

definitions.text: Given a chance to do business favourably
definitions.meaning: first meaning: involved in a venture from its start, on good terms
second meaning: the street-level storey of a shop

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is about investors who get in early; the literal sense is the level where a store's entrance is.
explanation.definitionFit: Early investors are said to get in at this level, and shoppers enter a store at street level.

clue.text: Record poem about cult hero

parts.note: 'If—' is Rudyard Kipling's famous poem
Che Guevara, the revolutionary whose face is a cult image

explanation.walkthrough: IF read backwards gives FI.

clue.text: Perform digital operation to cause somebody delight or embarrassment?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' suggests computers, but toes are digits too.

clue.text: Computer software has changed, right? We are mad

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written
